prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1328; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured reports that the vehicle was stopped at a red light when it was struck from behind.

Entry 2: Confirmed that the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was in force on the date of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates coverage.

Entry 3: Police report obtained. Responding officer confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the scene and records the collision as described by both drivers.

Entry 4: Statements taken from two independent witnesses. Both describe the impact the same way as the insured and say the other vehicle was moving too fast to stop.

Entry 5: Scene and vehicle photographs reviewed. The rear damage is largely consistent with the impact described, and no prior damage to the vehicle is known from the records available.

Entry 6: Other driver interviewed and does not dispute the sequence of events or the point of impact.

Entry 7: Claimant is represented by counsel. Initial medical report lists a wrist fracture, which is a typical injury for this type and force of impact, and there is no known prior injury to that area.

Entry 8: Claimant's account was revisited in a recorded follow-up. Some small details were added, but the core sequence of events has stayed the same across every statement.

Entry 9: Treatment records reviewed. Care followed a usual course, with activity restrictions and therapy easing as the claimant's condition improved.

Entry 10: Medical file shows steady recovery and a tapering off of treatment visits. Counsel has been copied on all updates requested for the bodily injury evaluation.

Entry 11: File reviewed and assessed as consistent across the police report, witness statements, photographs, vehicle damage and medical records. Claim moving to bodily injury evaluation.
